newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian mining official to be replaced - papers.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian mining official to be replaced - papers.

text.p: A top official in Indonesia's mines department responsible for handling the controversial Busang gold prospect is set to be replaced next week along with two other senior colleagues, media reports said on Saturday.

Three newspapers, Bisnis Indonesia, Media Indonesia and Harian Ekonomi Neraca, quoting unnamed sources in the ministry, said director-general for general mining Kuntoro Mangkusubroto would be replaced on Monday.

The newspapers, all Indonesian-language dailies, said director general for geological and mineral resources Adjat Sudradjat and director-general for electricity and energy development Zuhal would also be replaced.
The reports said the changes were approved by President Suharto in a presidential decree signed on Wednesday.
Official comment was not immediately available on Saturday.

Harian Ekonomi Neraca said Kuntoro's replacement would raise questions because of his key responsibility in handling the Busang gold deposit in East Kalimantan found by Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
Bisnis Indonesia said the reasons for the change were not clear.

Media Indonesia said it could be related to internal rivalries between a group of technocrats who once taught at the Bandung Institute of Technology and those loyal to Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana, a retired general.

Bre-X has said the Busang property in East Kalimantan province might hold less than the 71 million ounces of gold it had earlier declared. The original amount, worth $25 billion at current prices, would make it the gold find of the century.

Industry sources said this week that independent drilling tests of the Busang property were likely to be flown to Australia for analysis by mid-April with the results available by the end of the month.
Sudjana said on Wednesday there was gold at Busang but the actual amount had yet to be determined.
